title: [EPIC] Native task management when bd is not installed
description:
When bd (beads) is not initialized in a workspace, bdh should handle task management commands natively by talking to the aweb /v1/tasks API, instead of requiring bd to be installed.

## Context

Mia landed a full task management API in aweb (/v1/tasks): CRUD, claims, dependencies, ready-task filtering, project-scoped sequential numbering (slug-NNN). Alice is making the beads-specific code in beadhub optional. This epic covers the bdh CLI side.

## Design principle

Same interface, different backend. When bd IS initialized, pass through to bd as today (zero change to existing behavior). When bd is NOT initialized, bdh handles the commands itself via /v1/tasks. Agent instructions and muscle memory don't change — `bdh create`, `bdh ready`, `bdh close` work the same regardless of backend.

The : namespace stays for bdh-specific coordination features (chat, mail, status, etc). The passthrough commands get a native fallback.

## What the aweb /v1/tasks API covers today

### Available endpoints
- POST /v1/tasks — create task (title, description, notes, priority 0-4, type task|bug|feature, labels, parent_task_id, assignee_agent_id)
- GET /v1/tasks — list tasks (filters: status, assignee, type, priority, labels)
- GET /v1/tasks/ready — open tasks with no unresolved blockers
- GET /v1/tasks/{ref} — get task detail (includes blocked_by, blocks dependency info)
- PATCH /v1/tasks/{ref} — update task (any field; auto-assigns on in_progress, 409 if claimed by another, cascade-close descendants)
- DELETE /v1/tasks/{ref} — soft delete
- POST /v1/tasks/{ref}/deps — add dependency (with cycle detection)
- DELETE /v1/tasks/{ref}/deps/{dep_ref} — remove dependency

### ID format
Tasks use slug-NNN format (e.g., bdh-001, bdh-042). Refs can be UUID, integer, or slug-NNN.

### Notable behaviors
- Setting status=in_progress auto-assigns to the actor if unassigned, returns 409 if assigned to someone else
- Closing a parent task cascade-closes all descendants
- Dependencies have cycle detection
- Soft-delete (deleted_at timestamp, not hard delete)

### Gaps to fill (separate tasks/epics)
- **Comments**: Tasks have a single `notes` TEXT field, not threaded comments. Mia is adding a task_comments table. Agents use comments heavily for progress tracking.
- **Blocked endpoint**: No dedicated endpoint, but dependency info is in GET /v1/tasks/{ref}. bdh can compute this client-side.
- **Stats**: No endpoint yet. bdh can compute from list results.
- **Search**: List has filters but no free-text search.
- **Go SDK methods**: The aw Go SDK has no Task methods yet. bdh will need to add them (or call REST directly).

## bd commands to replicate (the important subset)

These are the commands agents use daily, per `bd prime` output and agent instructions:

### Must implement (P1)
1. `create --title="..." --type=task|bug|feature --priority=N` — map to POST /v1/tasks
2. `list --status=open|in_progress|closed` — map to GET /v1/tasks with filters
3. `show <ref>` — map to GET /v1/tasks/{ref}, display deps
4. `update <ref> --status=in_progress|open --title=... --description=... --notes=...` — map to PATCH /v1/tasks/{ref}
5. `close <ref> [<ref2> ...]` — map to PATCH /v1/tasks/{ref} with status=closed (loop for multiple)
6. `ready` — map to GET /v1/tasks/ready
7. `blocked` — compute client-side: list tasks that have open blockers (from dependency info)
8. `dep add <ref> <depends-on>` — map to POST /v1/tasks/{ref}/deps
9. `dep remove <ref> <dep-ref>` — map to DELETE /v1/tasks/{ref}/deps/{dep_ref}
10. `sync` — no-op in native mode (PostgreSQL is live). Print "nothing to sync (native mode)" or silent success.

### Should implement (P2)
11. `list --status=in_progress` with `--assignee` filter — agents check their active work
12. `comments <ref>` — view/add comments (depends on Mia's task_comments API)
13. `stats` — compute from list results (open/closed/blocked counts)
14. `reopen <ref>` — map to PATCH with status=open

### Won't implement (beads-specific, not needed)
- `sync` (JSONL upload) — goes away, PostgreSQL is authority
- `export` / `import` — beads-specific serialization
- `init` / `setup` / `hooks` — beads-local database setup
- `edit` — opens $EDITOR, agents already told not to use it
- `search` / `query` — free-text search, not critical for MVP
- `epic` / `swarm` / `mol` — advanced beads features
- `gate` / `merge-slot` — coordination features not used through tasks API
- `delete` — soft-delete available but not in standard agent workflow
- `promote` / `q` / `todo` — convenience wrappers
- `where` / `info` / `doctor` — beads-local diagnostics

## Architecture decisions

### Detection: bd vs native mode
Current flow in runPassthrough(): if .beadhub exists, load config and pass through to bd. 
New flow: check if bd is initialized (presence of .beads/ directory or `bd info` succeeds). If yes, pass through. If no, route to native handler.

### Go SDK vs direct REST
Two options:
A) Add Task methods to the aw Go SDK (aweb package) — clean, consistent with existing mail/chat/reservation patterns
B) Call REST directly from bdh — faster to implement, but duplicates HTTP/auth logic

Recommend Option A: add to aw SDK first, then use from bdh. This is how all other aweb features work.

### Output formatting
Native mode should match bd's output format closely enough that agent instructions work unchanged. Key formats:
- `create`: output the ref (e.g., "Created bdh-042")
- `list`: tabular output with ref, priority, type, status, title
- `show`: detailed view with description, deps, timestamps
- `ready`: same as list but filtered
- Support `--json` flag for structured output (agents sometimes use this)

### Coordination integration
In native mode, the existing coordination features (pre-flight check, auto-reserve, notifications) should still work. The pre-flight command check talks to beadhub, not bd — so it's independent of the backend.
close_reason: All 4 gaps implemented: --json flag, comments, dep list, --labels filter. 19 new tests total.

title: Detect bd-initialized vs native mode in passthrough
description:
Add detection logic to runPassthrough() to determine whether bd is initialized in the current workspace.

Current behavior: runPassthrough() always shells out to bd. If bd is not installed, it fails.

New behavior: before calling bd, check if bd is initialized (presence of .beads/ directory at git root). If not initialized, route to native task handler instead.

Key considerations:
- The check must be fast (filesystem stat, not running bd)
- If .beads/ exists, pass through to bd as today (zero behavior change)
- If .beads/ does not exist, route recognized commands to native handlers
- Unrecognized commands in native mode should error with a helpful message listing available commands
- The existing coordination features (pre-flight check, auto-reserve, notifications) should still work in native mode since they talk to beadhub, not bd

This is the routing layer — it doesn't implement any native commands, just decides which path to take.

title: Clean up stale same-host workspaces based on last_seen
description: detectGoneWorkspaces in notifications.go only deletes workspaces whose directory no longer exists. But agents commonly die without cleanup, leaving the directory intact — so their workspace and alias are stuck forever. Fix: extend detectGoneWorkspaces to also delete same-host workspaces that are offline longer than a threshold (default 4h). The server already returns last_seen_at in the workspace list response. Keep existing path-gone immediate delete. Add: path-exists + offline > threshold → delete. Same-host only (already hostname-filtered). Reported by alice.
close_reason: Approach was wrong — time-based cleanup is too aggressive since workspaces legitimately stay offline for days. Graceful deregister (bdh-26i.4) is the right fix.

title: [EPIC] Implement bdh :run autonomous agent loop
description: Implement bdh :run in this Go CLI as the autonomous wrapper described in Graces agent-loop SOT. The command should keep an AI coding agent continuously productive by looping through agent CLI invocations, exposing human terminal control, and later dispatching based on BeadHub coordination state. This epic tracks the MVP slice sequence agreed with Grace: Claude-only foundation first, terminal UX controls second, dispatch logic third, provider abstraction designed from the start but only Claude implemented initially.

External Python PoC exists at ../beadhub-grace/agent-loop.py and validates the stream-json loop mechanics. Grace requested one epic plus slice sub-beads, and generated work prompts must include a reminder to do a code-reviewer run before closing a bead.

title: Implement bdh :run slice 1: Claude loop foundation

This slice is the direct Go implementation of the proven mechanics from the Python prototype and should not yet depend on bdh-driven dispatch decisions.

title: Implement bdh :run slice 2: terminal control UX
description: Extend bdh :run so the human always has an open control channel during active runs and idle periods. Support /stop, /wait, /resume, and typed prompt injection with the pause semantics from the SOT: typing during a run should pause auto-dispatch after the current run completes until Enter submits the override prompt.

title: Implement bdh :run slice 3: bdh-driven dispatch logic
description: Teach bdh :run to query coordination state between runs and choose the next prompt by priority: pending chat first, unread mail second, current in-progress claim third, ready work fourth, and idle fallback last. Generated work prompts must include a reminder to perform a code-reviewer run before closing a bead.
design: Use existing bdh/API primitives where possible. This slice should introduce dispatch prompt construction and adaptive wait behavior without tying the loop to Claude-specific details.
close_reason: Implemented bdh-driven dispatch in :run with priority ordering for pending chat, unread mail, current claims, ready work, and idle fallback. The dispatcher builds work prompts with the required self-review/code-reviewer reminder and adjusts wait times by priority. title: Implement bdh :run slice 4: provider abstraction for future Codex support

design: Target interface per Graces SOT: BuildCommand(prompt, options) -> command + args; ParseOutput(line) -> structured event; SessionID(done_event) -> string; Capabilities() -> provider feature flags. The initial implementation should avoid premature complexity while keeping the contract stable.
close_reason: Implemented the provider abstraction as part of the initial :run foundation: BuildCommand, ParseOutput, SessionID, and Capabilities are defined behind a runProvider interface, with ClaudeProvider as the first implementation. title: Add bdh :list-active for cross-repo bead visibility
description:
## Context

bd only shows beads in the current repo. But a project may span multiple repos, and agents need to see what's happening across the whole project. bdh :list-active would query the server for all in-progress beads across all repos in the project.

## Proposed interface

bdh :list-active — show all in_progress beads across the project, grouped by repo
bdh :list-active --repo=<canonical-origin> — filter to specific repo
bdh :list-active --assignee=<alias> — filter by assignee

## Implementation

- Server already has all beads synced per project (POST /v1/bdh/sync uploads them).
- Need a new server endpoint (probably GET /v1/beads/active or extend GET /v1/beads/issues with filters).
- CLI command in bdh calls the endpoint and formats the output.
- Consider: should this also show claims (who's actively working on what)?

## Why it matters

This is table-stakes coordination visibility for multi-repo projects. "What's happening across my project" is a core question agents need answered.

title: Refactor chat command from flags to subcommands
description:
Refactor bdh :aweb chat from mutually exclusive flags to subcommands. The interface must be identical to aw CLI (which will also be updated to match).

Target interface (identical for both aw and bdh :aweb):
  chat send <alias> "message" [--start-conversation] [--leave-conversation] [--wait N] [--json]
  chat pending [--json]
  chat open <alias> [--json]
  chat history <alias> [--json]
  chat hang-on <alias> "message" [--json]

Design notes:
- Required arguments (alias, message) are positional, not flags
- Optional modifiers (--start-conversation, --leave-conversation, --wait) stay as flags
- Default send (no modifier) replaces the current --reply mode
- --leave-conversation (not --leaving) for consistency across both CLIs
- show-pending is out of scope
- The aw library API (chat.Send, chat.Open, etc.) does not change — this is CLI-only
- Embedded command strings in output formatting (lines 390, 411, 494, 584, 586) must also be updated

Files to modify (all in bdh repo):

close_reason: Fixed the bdh :run screen layout drift in commit 090c0d1. title: Add bdh :policy management commands (admin)
description:
## Context

Project policies (invariants + role playbooks) are currently managed via the API or dashboard. For CLI-first consistency, admins should be able to manage policies from the terminal.

## Proposed interface

bdh :policy — already exists, shows current policy (display needs fixing, see separate bead)
bdh :policy add --invariant --title="..." --guidance="..."
bdh :policy add --role --name="..." --playbook="..."
bdh :policy edit --invariant <id> --guidance="..."
bdh :policy edit --role <name> --playbook="..."
bdh :policy delete --invariant <id>
bdh :policy delete --role <name>

## Design considerations

- Admin-only: server must validate caller's role/permissions. Need to check if role-based authorization exists on the policy endpoints today.
- Content via flags (--guidance, --playbook) rather than opening an editor. CLAUDE.md says "Do NOT use bdh edit — it opens EDITOR which blocks agents." Same applies here — stdin or flags, never an interactive editor.
- Could also accept content from stdin for longer text: echo "..." | bdh :policy add --invariant --title="..." --guidance=-
- Server endpoints: check if PUT/DELETE exist on /v1/policies or if they need to be added to the beadhub server.

title: Add bdh :role command for agent role changes
description:
## Context

Currently agents pick a role during bdh :init and it's fixed. But agents may need to change roles (developer → reviewer, backend → frontend, etc.). The data model already supports role changes — role is NOT immutable (confirmed in beadhub-sot data-model.md and bdh-client.md which says "update workspace metadata including role if provided").

## Proposed interface

bdh :role — show current role and available roles
bdh :role <new-role> — change to a new role

## Implementation

- The workspace registration/update endpoint already accepts role updates.
- bdh :init already passes role to the server.
- This just needs a dedicated CLI command that calls the existing endpoint with a role update.
- Policy playbook changes automatically based on role — that's the whole point.
- Self-service: any agent can change their own role, no admin approval needed.

title: Fix policy display markdown formatting
description:
## Context

The output of bdh :policy displays project policies (invariants + role playbook) but the markdown formatting is broken. This is one of the first things a new user sees after onboarding — broken formatting gives a bad first impression.

## Investigation needed

- Check how the policy text is currently rendered in the CLI (internal/commands/ — likely the :policy command handler).
- Determine if the issue is: raw markdown dumped to terminal without rendering, incorrect whitespace/indentation, headers not visually distinct, code blocks mangled, or something else.
- Check if bdh uses any markdown-to-terminal rendering library, or if it just prints raw text.

## Fix

- Either render markdown properly for terminal output (using a Go library like glamour/charmbracelet), or format the output in a clean structured way without relying on markdown rendering.
- The output should be clean, readable, and make a good first impression.
